newsitem.title: UK: BNP plans North Korea debt issue.
newsitem.headline: BNP plans North Korea debt issue.

text.p: Banque Nationale de Paris said on Thursday it plans to issue North Korean debt certificates clearable through Euroclear and Cedel.
The issue, in the name of the NK Debt Corporation and expected to be around the equivalent of 400 million marks, will be in mark and Swiss france certificates.

"We believe a Euroclearable North Korean sovereign certificate will be very appealing for retail investors and a high percentage of the investment community," BNP senior trader Peter Bartlett told Reuters.
He anticipated the issue would trade at a premium of half to one percentage point over the normal secondary market price for North Korean debt, which is currently 30-1/2 cents in the dollar.
North Korean debt started the year at around 22/23 cents, rising along with other more so-called exotic sovereign debts as investors have sought out higher yielding emerging market paper.
North Korea's total commercial foreign debt, which is in default, is around $800 million.
Final distribution for the certificates will be due on March 7, 2010. Minimum denomination will be 80,000 marks or Swiss Francs with increments of 10,000 in either currency.
